newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dlr likely to remain strong in short term - ANZ.
newsitem.headline: NZ dlr likely to remain strong in short term - ANZ.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar will remain attractive to investors despite expectations of a lower Consumer Price Index (CPI) and Reserve Bank dissertations on the mix of monetary conditions, ANZ Bank said on Monday.

"Talk of ongoing issuing demand combined with seasonal local buying should limit any weakness to the recent US$0.6850/90 window and strength should see a test of 0.6970/7000," ANZ said in its weekly Market Focus.

It said the Kiwi's Trade-Weighted Index, which firmed to recent highs of 68.90 last week, should sustain this strength in the short term with a likely topside of 69.00/10 and a base of support at 68.50.
ANZ expects underlying inflation to be 0.4 percent in the March quarter, taking the annual rate down to 2.2 percent from 2.4 percent in the December year.

"A March quarter CPI result in line with our expectations may provide much needed reassurance to the financial markets that New Zealand is on track to achieve lower inflation over the year ahead," ANZ said.

"Regardless of the impact of increased government spending on the longer term inflation outlook, it may cause the markets to question why monetary conditions are tighter than the RBNZ requires at this time.
"This could lead to some retracement in short rates and/or the New Zealand dollar."
